written_by: sim/ owner, re-opening the wall and reconciling the null
one_line: The wall does not open because of TWO parameters, not one. t_bond_per_m decides whether glass leaves at all; the MULLION thresholds decide whether the opening is wider than the car. Lowering the mullion thresholds from 900/1400 to 40/120 costs the null literally nothing - the null bake is bit-identical - and turns a 2.15 x 4.55 m ragged blob into a full-height bay. The declared 9.6 m is not reachable by this impact at any setting, and that is the honest finding.

RECOMMENDED_CONFIGURATION.result: bay 4 vacated 96.8% BY AREA floor to head; mullion 5 travels 1.215 m and 2 of its segments detach; connected opening 2.15 x 6.00 m of glass, 3.80 x 6.00 m bridged across the departed mullion; 2,793 shards / 409 kg leave, 1,867 land on the floor.
RECOMMENDED_CONFIGURATION.picture: sim/out/gone_m1.png against sim/out/gone_sw_b100.png - LOOK AT THESE, they are the whole argument

WHY_THE_MULLION_THRESHOLDS_ARE_THE_MISSI.observation: across a 40x sweep of t_bond_per_m (4000, 1000, 400, 200, 100) mullions 3, 4, 6 and 7 never move more than 45 mm. Only MULLION 5 - the one the car hits head-on at y = 0 - responds at all.
WHY_THE_MULLION_THRESHOLDS_ARE_THE_MISSI.reason: the car proxy is 2.005 m wide and centred on y = 0, so it touches bays 4 and 5 and mullion 5 and nothing else. The only load path outward is glass -> edge clamp -> mullion 4 or 6, and the edge clamp breaks at an impulse of 2.5, which is instant. The glass lets go of its frame before the frame is loaded.
WHY_THE_MULLION_THRESHOLDS_ARE_THE_MISSI.dimensional_check: Blender passes breaking_threshold to Bullet's setBreakingImpulseThreshold, compared against the applied impulse in ONE substep. At 240 Hz x 8 substeps a threshold T is a sustained force of T x 1920 N. So mullion_joint 900 = 1.73 MN and mullion_base 1400 = 2.69 MN. A 75 x 160 mm 6063-T6 extrusion fails in bending at roughly 30 kN and its base studs in shear at roughly 200 kN, i.e. T = 16 and T = 104. The shipped numbers are 55x and 13x too strong.
WHY_THE_MULLION_THRESHOLDS_ARE_THE_MISSI.what_40_120_does: mullion 5 goes from 0.147 m of bend to 1.215 m and two segments leave; bay 4 goes from 58.2% to 96.8% vacated by area; the connected opening goes from 2.15 x 4.55 m to 2.15 x 6.00 m (3.80 x 6.00 bridged).

THE_NULL_SURVIVES_IT_BY_NOT_BEING_ON_THA.method: blender -b -P sim/build_breach_sim.py -- --frames 480 --bake --no-car --wake-all, i.e. every body AWAKE at frame 1 for 2.0 s of world time under gravity with nothing to hit it. Twice as long as the 240-frame null the shipped threshold was chosen against.

table.note: BIT-IDENTICAL to null_b100 on every statistic. The mullion thresholds are never approached under dead load; frame bodies move 0.175 mm.
THE NULL BREAKS. 15/50 is below the dead-load margin and the wall begins to shed itself.

THE_NULL_SURVIVES_IT_BY_NOT_BEING_ON_THA.the_bracket: 40/120 opens the wall and leaves the null untouched; 15/50 destroys the null. There is a clean 3x window and 40/120 sits in it with 900/1400 above it doing nothing for the null.
THE_NULL_SURVIVES_IT_BY_NOT_BEING_ON_THA.THE_TRADE_THAT_WAS_MADE_DID_NOT_BUY_WHAT: over the same 480 frames the SHIPPED threshold of 4000 has a median displacement of 15.21 mm against 100's 8.48, and 264 shards over 50 mm against 100's 5. It is worse on the wall as a whole. All 4000 buys is the binary 'nothing over 0.25 m', and it buys that by making the glass unbreakable - which is exactly the failure mode 'a null that passes because nothing can move'. A stiffer constraint network is HARDER for 24 sequential-impulse iterations to satisfy, not easier.

the_three_shards_that_do_leave_at_100.name: GS_b06_00010
the_three_shards_that_do_leave_at_100.reading: an unclamped 0.68 kg cell 0.4 m above the sill, held only by its bonds. It moves faster than free fall in the first 9 frames, so this is an initialisation kick, not gravity.

the_three_shards_that_do_leave_at_100.name: GS_b05_01261
the_three_shards_that_do_leave_at_100.reading: two large CLAMPED cells on the mullion 6 line whose 2.5 clamp holds for 1.2 s and then creeps out. Their static load is 28 N = 0.0148 N.s per substep, 170x under the threshold, so this is accumulated solver drift in a 14,075-constraint island, not a threshold being exceeded.

THE_NULL_SURVIVES_IT_BY_NOT_BEING_ON_THA.honest_status: the null does NOT fully pass at the recommended configuration. 3 shards of 3,796 leave and the panes that stay sag 11.5 px. But it does not fully pass at the SHIPPED configuration either (10.75 px on bay 7), and it never did - the old instrument charged bay 2 at the wrong range and therefore reported bay 2 as the worst bay when bay 7 is. Nothing regressed; a broken instrument was hiding the state of things.

APERTURE_AND_FRAGMENT_ENERGY_WERE_NEVER_.claim_tested: 'at threshold 100 the fragments leave at 2.4x the impactor speed, and aperture size and fragment energy share one parameter'
APERTURE_AND_FRAGMENT_ENERGY_WERE_NEVER_.finding: they do not share one parameter. Across the 40x bond sweep the fragment energy statistics are FLAT:

field_KE_max_J.note: 100 is the LOWEST of the four and 400 the highest - not monotone, i.e. noise, not a trend

peak_speed_any_shard_ms.note: the same peak exists in the SHIPPED bake where nothing leaves the wall

APERTURE_AND_FRAGMENT_ENERGY_WERE_NEVER_.where_the_extreme_speeds_come_from: not the car. The 200 fastest shards peak a MEDIAN of 0.125 s after impact at a median 1.27 m BEHIND the car's rear plane; the single fastest, GS_b04_00502, hits 137.6 m/s at frame 261 = impact +0.4875 s, at x = 17.26 while the car nose is at x = 23.25 - six metres past it - and it is travelling BACKWARDS, toward the wall. 66 shards peak on that same frame. Nothing physical throws a shard backwards at 137 m/s six metres behind the impactor.
APERTURE_AND_FRAGMENT_ENERGY_WERE_NEVER_.the_car_proxy_is_not_the_source: its surface never moves faster than it does. Probes at the nose tip, rear wing tip, rear wing corner and airbox all report 9.64..19.90 m/s, identical to the origin, because the animated pitch has settled by frame 255. Controls: the origin probe returns the car's own speed exactly, and with rotation zeroed every probe agrees to 4.3e-13 m/s.
APERTURE_AND_FRAGMENT_ENERGY_WERE_NEVER_.what_it_actually_is: a contact/constraint blow-up in the debris field well downstream of the wall, present at EVERY threshold including the shipped one. It affects 0.02% of the field by mass (64 shards of ~10 g over 100 m/s out of 2,240 kg).
APERTURE_AND_FRAGMENT_ENERGY_WERE_NEVER_.the_honest_energy_number: LAUNCH speed - each shard's speed at the frame it first passes 0.25 m from home, mass-weighted - is p50 5.85, p90 14.5, p99 23.4 m/s at bond 100, i.e. 1.43x the 16.4 m/s impactor at the 99th percentile by mass. That is a defensible number for glass driven by an infinitely massive kinematic body, where the free-particle bound is (1+e)v. The '2.4x' figure was a max over 3,948 bodies of a statistic dominated by the downstream blow-up.
APERTURE_AND_FRAGMENT_ENERGY_WERE_NEVER_.so: the aperture can be opened without touching fragment energy, because the parameter that opens it never controlled the energy. What SHOULD be fixed is the downstream blow-up, and that is a contact/solver issue, not a threshold.

THE_DECLARED_9.6_m_IS_NOT_REACHABLE_BY_T.what_9.6_means: mullion_intact.breach_state(): 'The aperture is 9.6 m wide on the launch axis (|Y| <= 4.8), so the three inside it go, and the two ON its edge fold.' Mullions at |y| < 3.0 (y = -2.2, 0, +2.2) destroyed; at 3.0 <= |y| < 5.0 (y = +-4.4) bent.
THE_DECLARED_9.6_m_IS_NOT_REACHABLE_BY_T.the_glass_ceiling: bays 3,4,5,6 span y = -4.385 .. +4.385 = 8.77 m of GLASS. Reaching 9.6 m of glass needs 385 mm off the inner edge of bays 2 and 7, which the same plan marks `retained`. So 9.6 m is the clear span between the two BENT mullions, a different object from the glass aperture, and the two were being compared to each other.
THE_DECLARED_9.6_m_IS_NOT_REACHABLE_BY_T.the_impact_ceiling: the car proxy is 2.005 m wide. Only bays 4 and 5 and mullion 5 are ever touched. No setting of bond, mullion or clamp thresholds moved mullions 4 or 6 more than 45 mm, because the load path to them runs through a 2.5-impulse edge clamp that fails instantly.
THE_DECLARED_9.6_m_IS_NOT_REACHABLE_BY_T.experiment_that_settles_it: m4 = bond 100, mullion 40/120, glass edge clamp raised 2.5 -> 25 (10x) to make the pane keep hold of its frame long enough to load mullions 4 and 6. It made the aperture WORSE, not wider: vacated 18.4% -> 7.5%, connected hole 2.15 x 6.00 -> 1.65 x 2.05 m, and mullions 4 and 6 still moved 4 mm and 7 mm. A stronger clamp holds more glass in the wall; it does not transmit more load to the neighbouring mullions.
THE_DECLARED_9.6_m_IS_NOT_REACHABLE_BY_T.conclusion: a 2.0 m car at 16.4 m/s makes an opening about one bay wide plus the mullion it strikes: 3.80 x 6.00 m. The 9.6 x 5.6 m is an art-direction target, not a consequence of this impact. Closing the gap needs a decision, not a parameter: widen the impact event, script mullions 4 and 6 to fail (breach_state() already DECLARES them destroyed, so declaring is already what is happening), or re-declare the aperture at what the impact makes.

sim/aperture.py.what: the aperture measured as a CONNECTED region on a 25 mm raster of the wall plane, with the mullion strips passable only where that mullion segment has actually left.
sim/aperture.py.why: build_breach_sim.aperture_report() takes the bbox of the ORIGINS of everything that moved.
sim/aperture.py.the_control_that_fires: TRAP_two_corners - two lone shards at opposite corners of the glazing. The old measure reports a 13.01 x 5.79 m aperture off those two shards. This one reports 0.20 x 0.25 m.
sim/aperture.py.other_controls: POS_all_gone recovers the full 77.4 m2 glazed area at 100% fill; NEG_none_gone returns 0; SHAPE_3x2m recovers a synthetic window and correctly splits it at the mullion.

sim/sagpx.py.what: sag in pixels, per shard per frame, through the applied scene's own animated camera track. Nothing is multiplied across frames.
sim/sagpx.py.controls: PROJECTOR - the breach centre must land at (1920, 1080); SCALE - one pixel's worth of metres must read 1.000 px; ZERO; OFFSCREEN. All four fire.
sim/sagpx.py.a_finding_from_the_control_itself: the applied-scene report says the camera looks straight at the breach centre at frame 2834. It does not. At 2834 the breach centre is 42.5 deg off axis and projects at x = 51 px, one screen-width from centre. The frame at which this camera actually points at the breach is 2901: 0.00 deg, 0.0 px error, 595.1 m.

sim/build_breach_sim.py::camera_ranges.was: the nearest beat-sheet camera KEY to the bay's CENTRE over the whole take, with no test of whether the bay was in the frame or whether the frame was after release.
sim/build_breach_sim.py::camera_ranges.now: the applied scene's own transform at all 2,978 frames, the bay sampled on a 5x5 grid, every sample tested against the 3840x2160 raster, frames before release excluded.
sim/build_breach_sim.py::camera_ranges.consequence: every pixel figure taken through bay 2 was 6.5x too big, which is where 7.1 px came from.

INSTRUMENTS_BUILT_OR_FIXED.sim/breach_metrics.py: one scorer run identically on every bake, carrying its own positive and negative controls in every report.
INSTRUMENTS_BUILT_OR_FIXED.a_control_of_my_own_that_failed_first: selecting 'bodies that never moved' by net displacement < 1e-6 m is wrong: GS_b04_01485 in the b100 bake leaves at 18 m/s and lands back within 2.5e-7 m of home, so the negative control read 6.69 m/s. THE_SAG_RE_MEASURED.instruction_followed: re-measured AFTER the wall was fixed, with the corrected instrument, as instructed.
THE_SAG_RE_MEASURED.THE_WORST_BAY_IS_BAY_7_NOT_BAY_2: bay 7 is filmed from 7.58 m where one 4K pixel is 2.548 mm; bay 2 from 22.87 m where it is 7.607 mm. Bay 2 was only ever the worst bay because the old code charged it at 3.52 m. Every previous decision about the sag was taken on the wrong bay.
THE_SAG_RE_MEASURED.so_what_it_costs: the criterion is 1 px on the panes that stay. It is missed by 11.5x at the recommended configuration and by 10.8x at the shipped one. This is NOT a regression - it has never been met - and it is a SOLVER-ITERATION defect, not a threshold defect: creep_vs_ring reports CREEP with a drift of 5.24 mm over 2.0 s, and the file's own note at line 131 already said 3,948 bodies in one constraint island is more than 24 sequential-impulse iterations can hold rigid.
THE_SAG_RE_MEASURED.caveat: these are --wake-all figures, deliberately harsher than the shipping configuration, in which the wall is start_deactivated and measures 0.000 m until the impact wakes it.

THE_f0866_SLAB_ARTEFACT.asked: the coordinator rendered f0858/f0862/f0866/f0880 and found a soup of overlapping hard-edged translucent slabs at f0866, hypothesis: the intact pane and the shards both render for ~12 frames.
THE_f0866_SLAB_ARTEFACT.HYPOTHESIS_FALSIFIED: no frame renders both. apply_breach.py keys the pane's hide_render CONSTANT at [1, r-1, r] -> [0,0,1] and every shard's at [1, r-1, r] -> [1,1,0] with r = min(release) over that bay. Read off breach_film.npz: every fractured bay's pane hides at 860 and its shards appear at 860. The ONLY exception is 9 shards in bays 5 and 7 that appear at 861 - a 9-shard, ONE-frame HOLE, not a double. That cannot make a 12-frame whole-wall artefact.
THE_f0866_SLAB_ARTEFACT.WHAT_IT_ACTUALLY_IS: the shard field itself. I projected the bay rectangles through the real camera onto the f0866 render (sim/tmp/f0866_bays.png): the slabs lie exactly inside the destroyed bays 3/4/5 and stop at their boundaries. At f0866 bay 4's shards are a median 559 mm from home, spread over 1.4 m of DEPTH (x = 14.95..16.35), and displaced a median 259 px / max 604 px on screen - while bay 7, which does not move, shows 5.7 mm and 1.3 px. The independent elevation drawing from the same table (sim/out/wall_f0866.png) shows bays 4 and 5 fully outboard at that instant.
THE_f0866_SLAB_ARTEFACT.AND_IT_IS_A_SYMPTOM_OF_THE_DEFECT_I_WAS_: at t_bond_per_m 4000 the pane bulges 1.65 m outboard AS A SHEET and springs back - by f900 bay 4's median depth offset is back to 17 mm from 483 mm at f866. So the take contains a shatter-and-un-shatter: ~3,000 flat glass plates spread through a metre of depth, seen through one another, then reassembling. That is what 'hard-edged translucent slabs, several deep, at multiple orientations' is.
THE_f0866_SLAB_ARTEFACT.the_prediction_to_test: at the recommended configuration the glass in bay 4 LEAVES instead of returning, so the stack should not form and should not un-form. Re-render f0855-f0890 after the re-bake and re-apply, exactly as instructed. If slabs survive that, it is a second defect.

THE DOCSTRING OF build_breach_sim.py IS WRONG ABOUT THE GLASS MASS. It says 'an F1 car is 798 kg against 4.9 kg of glass per pane'. A pane is 2.17 x 6.025 m of 11.5 mm laminate = 375 kg, and the six fractured bays total 2,240.9 kg in the sim's own shard_meta. The simulated masses are right; the sentence justifying the kinematic car proxy is wrong by 75x. The car carries 13,087 kg.m/s and the shard field takes up to 5,946 kg.m/s of it - 45% - so the claim that the honest car response is 'a few mm/s' is not supported.

proposed_defect_log_entries_R2_092_to_R2.the_scene: n_GW_Right_Glass = 0 on film9, film10, film11 and film11_r2085cam. work/lighting/f860_full_a6.png shows bare aluminium bars with the paddock, pit wall and grandstand visible through them. Beats 1-3 are the showroom, so this is roughly a third of a film with no cuts.
proposed_defect_log_entries_R2_092_to_R2.the_cause: tools/build_film_scene.py executes sim/apply_breach.py's own requirement R3 and deletes GW_Right_Glass_00..09. It is right to. R3 is written on the understanding that apply_breach supplies the replacement, and it does - GP_b00..GP_b09, all ten bays. But apply_breach is a separate invocation on an already-built blend and the joiner cannot know whether it was ever run, so every world rebuild ships a film with the panes deleted and nothing put back.
proposed_defect_log_entries_R2_092_to_R2.THE_HALF_THAT_MATTERS_MOST: THE METRIC COULD NEVER HAVE REPORTED IT HEALTHY. n_GW_Right_Glass is a name-prefix count of ROUND ONE's object names. The replacements are called GP_b*. It reads 0 for a correctly applied scene exactly as it reads 0 for an empty wall. Anyone who checked it and saw 0 would conclude 'no glass' whether or not glass was there - and anyone who FIXED the glass would have seen the number not move. A metric that cannot distinguish the fixed state from the broken one does not merely fail to catch the defect; it actively teaches everyone who reads it that the fix did nothing. That is why this survived four film builds.
proposed_defect_log_entries_R2_092_to_R2.fix: sim/apply_breach.py::east_wall_census counts GP_b* by bay, evaluates their hide_render curves at frame 1, and REFUSES to write the scene if the east wall has no glass in it. Six controls, including the defect itself (all ten panes missing), a pane that exists but is hidden at frame 1, and the same pane visible at frame 41 which must NOT be charged.

proposed_defect_log_entries_R2_092_to_R2.title: R5's glazing-pocket check tested vertices, so eleven solid mullions lying through the pocket reported `clear` on 29,387 meshes
proposed_defect_log_entries_R2_092_to_R2.detail: R5 requires that nothing occupy x 14.9455..14.9695, because 'a solid mullion or sill laid through it starts every clamped shard inside metal'. It tested VERTICES. Round 1's east mullions are solid boxes spanning x 14.920..15.080 - straight through the 24 mm pocket - with all eight vertices outside it. An edge test does not fix it either: the x-running edges sit at z 0.0 and 6.2 and the z-running edges at x 14.920 and 15.080, so not one of the twelve edges enters the pocket. What passes through is the side FACES.
proposed_defect_log_entries_R2_092_to_R2.fix: triangle-vs-box by the separating-axis theorem after the same AABB pre-filter, run twice: once against the whole pocket and once against the bays' CLEAR OPENINGS. Only the clear-opening arm refuses, because the 22.5 mm captured edge is what a glazing pocket is FOR. Eleven controls. On world/verify_showroom.blend it lists exactly the eleven mullions plus sill and head as capture-band, and refuses on round 1's three transoms at z 1.35/2.85/4.35, which really are bars across the picture.

proposed_defect_log_entries_R2_092_to_R2.title: the release rule existed in two places that disagreed, and BOTH were wrong: one shatters the wall seven frames before the car touches it, the other renders an intact pane over glass 350 mm out of place
proposed_defect_log_entries_R2_092_to_R2.why_it_is_dangerous: release is the frame apply_breach hides a bay's intact pane and shows its shards. It is the single frame the wall breaks on, in a film with no cuts. Two entry points to the same pipeline computed it differently and neither was checked against the other.
proposed_defect_log_entries_R2_092_to_R2.rule_1: resample.main() called release_frames(frames, loc) - 0.2 mm from the FIRST frame of the table. THIS IS THE PATH A LOCAL BAKE TAKES, because a local build writes only the raw table and resample is a separate step. On a wall that creeps 0.4 mm under its own weight before the car arrives it fires SEVEN FRAMES EARLY: the wall shatters while the car is still metres away and nothing in the transform table looks wrong.
proposed_defect_log_entries_R2_092_to_R2.rule_2: remote_bake.py measured 2 mm from the state AT the impact frame. It fixes rule 1 and introduces the opposite error, silently. ONE FILM FRAME SPANS THE WHOLE IMPACT - f859 is 36.5 ms before contact, f860 is 5.1 ms after, and in between bay 4's glass moves a median 128.9 mm and a maximum 350.2 mm. Referencing AT f860 measures that as zero, waits for a further 2 mm, and fires at 861. Measured on the shipped bake: rule 1 gives min 860, rule 2 gives min 861.
proposed_defect_log_entries_R2_092_to_R2.MY_OWN_FIRST_FIX_WAS_WRONG: I unified on rule 2, on the strength of its written justification, and committed it. That would have made the shipped behaviour WORSE by one frame - an intact pane rendering over glass a third of a metre out of place, on the frame the wall breaks. The coordinator's instruction to write this up with its own controls is what made me measure it against the real bake instead of trusting the comment.
proposed_defect_log_entries_R2_092_to_R2.rule_3_the_actual_rule: reference the last film frame STRICTLY BEFORE contact (floor of the impact frame, not round), 2 mm threshold. Referencing before contact keeps the impact's first frame visible; referencing at contact rather than at the table start makes it immune to whatever the wall did while it was waiting. Fires at 860 on the shipped bake and at the impact on the synthetic creep.
proposed_defect_log_entries_R2_092_to_R2.controls: six in resample.selftest, including the one that condemns rule 2: a synthetic 129 mm step across the impact frame followed by only 0.5 mm more, which rule 2 NEVER fires on at all, and which rule 3 fires on at the impact frame.

WHICH_OF_MY_MEASUREMENTS_CAME_THROUGH_IT.the_shipped_table_did: sim/out/breach_film.json has no `release_reference_frame` key, which remote_bake always writes, so sim/out/breach_film.npz was produced by rule 1 - the dangerous path.
WHICH_OF_MY_MEASUREMENTS_CAME_THROUGH_IT.and_it_was_not_bitten: MEASURED, not assumed: over film frames 845..859 the maximum displacement of ANY body in the shipped bake is 0.000000 mm. The shipping configuration is start_deactivated, so the wall is asleep until the impact wakes it and there is no creep for a 0.2 mm trigger to catch. Rule 1 and rule 3 both give a minimum release of 860 on this bake.
WHICH_OF_MY_MEASUREMENTS_CAME_THROUGH_IT.so_which_results_are_suspect: none of the numbers in this report. Everything I measured - the aperture, the slab depth and alignment profiles, the gone fractions by count and by area, the blow-up population - is computed from transforms and shard origins and does not read the release column at all. The two things that DO read it are verify_breach --swap (whose subject IS the release spread) and apply_breach's swap frames, and both were computed from the shipped table under rule 1, which on this bake agrees with rule 3 at 860.
WHICH_OF_MY_MEASUREMENTS_CAME_THROUGH_IT.what_WOULD_have_been_suspect: any bake run with --wake-all, or any future bake where start_deactivated is off, resampled through the local path. The wake-all nulls the threshold decision was made against creep 5 to 15 mm. They were never resampled - they were scored directly from the raw table - so the decision is unaffected. But that is luck, not design.

DEFECT_NUMBER_RENUMBERING.why: the eight findings below were first proposed as R2-066..073. Every one of those numbers was already taken while this work was in flight: R2-066/067/068 are beat 2's and the continuity gate's, R2-070/071/072/073 are the socket sweep's and the importers'. The block issued to the breach is R2-092..R2-099 and that is what these are now.
DEFECT_NUMBER_RENUMBERING.note: docs/DEFECT-LOG-R2.md is not mine to edit; these are proposals for the log's owner.

THE_EAST_WALL__handed_to_me_by_the_film_.the_report: n_GW_Right_Glass = 0. R3 deletes round 1's ten panes and nothing supplies replacements, so beats 1-3 render an open wall.
THE_EAST_WALL__handed_to_me_by_the_film_.CONFIRMED_AND_SEEN: work/lighting/f860_full_a6.png, a render of the current joiner output. The east wall is a row of bare pale aluminium bars at 2.2 m centres with the paddock, pit wall and grandstand visible straight through the gaps. No glass, and therefore none of the glass reflections beat 1 spends 33 seconds on. I looked at it.
THE_EAST_WALL__handed_to_me_by_the_film_.THE_CAUSE_IS_NOT_A_BUG_IN_ANY_ONE_STEP: tools/build_film_scene.py executes sim/apply_breach.py's OWN requirement R3 and deletes GW_Right_Glass_00..09. It is right to: they are zero-thickness planes on x = 15.000, 33.5 mm proud of where the glass really is, and two east walls that close together z-fight through beat 1. R3 is written on the understanding that apply_breach supplies the replacement - and it does, GP_b00..GP_b09, ALL TEN BAYS including the four the car never touches. But apply_breach is a SEPARATE invocation on an already-built blend and the joiner cannot know whether it was ever run. film9 was applied once, at 15:01. film10, film11 and film11_r2085cam never were.
THE_EAST_WALL__handed_to_me_by_the_film_.WHY_THE_METRIC_COULD_NOT_HAVE_CAUGHT_IT: n_GW_Right_Glass is a name-prefix count of ROUND ONE's names. The replacements are called GP_b*. It reads 0 for a correctly applied scene exactly as it does for an empty wall. A number that cannot tell the fixed state from the broken one.
THE_EAST_WALL__handed_to_me_by_the_film_.WHAT_I_DID: sim/apply_breach.py now takes an east-wall census AFTER building and REFUSES to write the file if the wall has no glass in it at frame 1. Six controls including the defect itself. The panes are restored by the re-apply, which is the same operation as landing the new bake - they are not two jobs.
THE_EAST_WALL__handed_to_me_by_the_film_.AND_A_SECOND_THING_THAT_IS_WORSE: the aluminium in the scene is ROUND ONE's. GW_Right_Mull_00..10, _Sill, _Head, _Transom_0/1/2, _BaseReveal - 26 objects the joiner keeps and nothing in round 2 touches. Three things are wrong with it and all three are visible: it is a solid box x 14.920..15.080, so it stands 80 mm EAST of the breach plane that mullion_intact.section() says nothing may cross; its transoms are at z 1.35/2.85/4.35 against the sim's 1.60/3.10/4.60, 250 mm out; and IT NEVER MOVES, because R6 is unfulfilled and the 152 MUL*/TRN* transforms in the table have nothing to bind to.
THE_EAST_WALL__handed_to_me_by_the_film_.SEEN: render/breach_f9/f9_1920_f0880.png. The car is already outside on the forecourt and the east wall is a spiderweb of crack lines in a still-flat sheet, with a dead-straight undeformed aluminium grid across the whole aperture. It reads as a cracked windscreen, not a breach. That single frame is the shipped 4000 configuration and R6 in one picture.
THE_EAST_WALL__handed_to_me_by_the_film_.THE_GEOMETRY_IS_NOT_MINE: world/items/mullion_intact.py builds the real extrusion and declares breach_state(); mullion_bent_stub is manifest item 108 and does not exist as code. Nothing in world/ or tools/ imports mullion_intact for geometry at all - the only importers are sim/fracture.py and sim/breachlib.py, and they read the interface JSON. Closing R6 means building segmented mullion geometry and that belongs to world/items/, not here.

R5_RE_RUN_ON_REAL_GEOMETRY.WHAT_THIS_MEANS_FOR_THE_RE_APPLY: the apply will REFUSE on the current film scene, and the refusal is TRUE.  It is not about the glass I am restoring; it is about round 1's frame still being the frame.  Closing it properly is R6 - build the real segmented mullions and transoms from world/items/ and delete round 1's - and that geometry is not mine.  So the re-apply is done with --force, deliberately, with sim/out/preflight_pocket_R5.json saved alongside naming every intruder.  That is what --force is for and it is the only use of it here.
R5_RE_RUN_ON_REAL_GEOMETRY.the_alternative_I_rejected: scoping the pocket so the transoms stop registering.  That would make the check pass by making it blind again, which is the whole defect it was just fixed for.

THE_SECOND_SEED__started_not_finished.why_the_sweep_was_single_seeded: not a decision. sim/fracture.py's main() hard-coded the output path, so the only way to make a second plan was to overwrite sim/out/fracture_wall.npz - the plan every baked table, every applied scene and every instrument is keyed to BY SHARD ID. It would have silently re-numbered 3,796 shards under a bake that still referred to the old ones. Fixed: fracture.py now takes --out, and its help says what the default does, because the default is the dangerous one.
THE_SECOND_SEED__started_not_finished.seed_2_plan_built: sim/tmp/fracture_wall_seed2.npz, seed 20260804 against the shipping 20260803. Free: the plan build is pure numpy and takes seconds.

WHAT_IT_ALREADY_ANSWERS_WITHOUT_A_BAKE.reading: the two plans are the same plan to within a per cent on every count that drives the sim. Bay 4 differs by 2 shards in 1,531 and its clamped count is IDENTICAL at 227, as is bay 5's at 209. So the fracture plan is NOT where the run-to-run variance lives, and a second seed will be a test of the SOLVER given a plan, not of the plan. That is worth knowing before spending the bake.

THE_SECOND_SEED__started_not_finished.STILL_NOT_DONE: the seed-2 BAKE. It is a 300-frame run at the recommended configuration, about 30 minutes of one core, and the command is: blender -b --factory-startup -P sim/build_breach_sim.py -- --shards sim/tmp/fracture_wall_seed2.npz --frames 300 --bake --out sim/tmp/s2.blend --export sim/tmp/s2.npz --report sim/tmp/s2.json, then sim/breach_metrics.py on the pair. It was not run because the box has one core free and the 1,657-frame bake owns it, and because the farm's exec refuses to deploy over a running render, which it was doing.
THE_SECOND_SEED__started_not_finished.what_the_seed_2_bake_would_settle: whether the 96.8 % / 97.8 % vacated figure for bay 4 is a property of the impact or of one particular set of crack lines. Given how close the two plans are, I expect it to be the impact - but that is a prediction and it has not been tested.

R2_096_THE_DOWNSTREAM_BLOW_UP__RE_MEASUR.A_CORRECTION_TO_THE_INHERITED_RECORD: GS_b04_00502 at 137.6 m/s on frame 261 is NOT in the shipped bake. It is in sim/tmp/sw_b100.npz, the bond-100 sweep point. In the SHIPPED bake that shard peaks at 70.5 m/s on frame 243. Two bakes were being quoted as one.

AND_THE_SHIPPED_CONFIGURATION_IS_THE_WOR.reading: the change I am applying reduces the blow-up population by 7.6x. It was recorded as happening 'at every threshold including the shipped one', which is true, but not at every threshold EQUALLY. This is an argument FOR the change that nobody had.

worst.f863: 410 shards simultaneously over 60 m/s, all 410 in raster

IT_IS_ON_SCREEN.occlusion: at f863, 291 of 410 are NOT behind the car proxy. At f888-891, none are.
IT_IS_ON_SCREEN.and_they_are_not_hidden: all 828 have release frame 860, so they render from the swap onward.

WHAT_IT_DRAWS.method: 180 deg shutter = half a film frame of world time, through the applied scene's own camera track, on the decimated film table (decimation error 0.00000 m on these shards)
WHAT_IT_DRAWS.THE_CONTROL_THAT_DECIDES_HOW_BAD_IT_IS: the same measurement on the ORDINARY shards on the same frames: median 34-77 px against the blow-up's 69-155. It is 2 to 3 times the correct field's streak, not a hundred times. A distinctly longer dash among many dashes, not a lone scar on a still wall.
WHAT_IT_DRAWS.not_a_2p9_m_streak: a sustained 137 m/s shard would cover 2.85 m in an unramped exposure, but the spike lasts 2-3 sim frames (8-12 ms) and is aliased by the 1/24 s sampling, so the rendered travel is 0.23-0.44 m.

WHERE_IT_COMES_FROM__what_the_data_suppo.the_discriminator_is_POSITION: bays 4 and 5 only, origins in the bottom metre (z 0.091..0.730 in bays that run to 6.067). 52.6% of every bay-4/5 shard originating below z = 0.30 m blows up. Mass is not the discriminator (median 10.38 g against the bays' 11.34 g) and neither is the clamp flag (253 clamped, 575 not).
WHERE_IT_COMES_FROM__what_the_data_suppo.it_is_a_ramp_not_a_step: the fastest shard runs 13.8 -> 31.3 -> 52.2 -> 103.6 -> 137.1 -> 116.3 -> 5.7 m/s over seven sim frames while x goes 16.10 -> 16.32 -> 15.21. Accelerate, reverse, stop dead. That is a constraint/contact resolution signature, not a collision.

TWO_clusters_not_one.A: sim frames 175-176, 480 shards, nearest proxy part tyre_FR or nose, and 102 of the 480 are INSIDE a proxy part by up to 37 mm. A 0.15 mm collision margin against 8.5 mm of car travel per substep is a plausible capture-then-eject.
TWO_clusters_not_one.B: sim frames 243-252, 348 shards up to 106.5 m/s, nearest car part at a MEDIAN 1.02 m. No car contact, no neighbour contact, no ground contact. Nothing measured explains cluster B.

WHERE_IT_COMES_FROM__what_the_data_suppo.ruled_out: the ground (zero shards below the sill top), a shard jam (nearest-neighbour p5 9.0 mm, zero pairs under the 0.15 mm margin), and mass.

correlation_of_penetration_with_peak_spe.reading: far too weak to call penetration the cause, and 378 of cluster A's 480 are not penetrating at all.

R2_096_THE_DOWNSTREAM_BLOW_UP__RE_MEASUR.STILL_NOT_EXPLAINED: cluster B. 348 shards reaching 106 m/s with no contact of any kind that can be measured from baked transforms. A released bond impulse is the only candidate and it is untested - the bond-clustering test scores 0.999 for blow-up shards but 0.875 for a random contiguous patch, so it is barely above what adjacency gives for free.
R2_096_THE_DOWNSTREAM_BLOW_UP__RE_MEASUR.AND_A_FIGURE_THAT_REFRAMES_THE_FIELD: the MEDIAN shard in the whole field peaks at 38.9 m/s = 2.4x the 16.4 m/s impactor, 59.0% exceed 2x, and 71.1% exceed the free-particle bound (1+e)v = 18.7 m/s. The previous agent's 1.43x is the LAUNCH speed at the 99th percentile by mass, which is a different and also correct statistic. Both are true and they answer different questions: the field is launched at a defensible speed and then something makes most of it much faster afterwards.
R2_096_THE_DOWNSTREAM_BLOW_UP__RE_MEASUR.not_seen: every 'visible' claim here is a projection through the camera track, not a look at an image. It has not been rendered.
